# Remove accidentally tracked generated files safely

Use the first section for normal cleanup. It keeps local files and only stops
tracking them from this commit forward.

Avoid history rewriting unless you really need the files removed from old
commits too. History rewriting changes commit IDs and requires force pushing.


## Safe cleanup: stop tracking, keep local files

This is the right command for `.venv`, `__pycache__`, build folders, logs, etc.

```sh
git rm -r --cached .venv __pycache__
printf "\n.venv/\n__pycache__/\n*.pyc\n" >> .gitignore
git add .gitignore
git commit -m "stop tracking generated files"
git push origin main
```

`--cached` means "remove from Git index only". The local files remain on disk.


## History rewrite: only if old commits must be cleaned too

Do this only after the safe cleanup is committed and pushed. Make a fresh clone
or a full backup first. Do not run this with an empty target.

```sh
TARGET=".venv"

if [ -z "$TARGET" ]; then
  echo "TARGET is empty; aborting" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -e "$TARGET" ]; then
  echo "TARGET does not exist locally; aborting: $TARGET" >&2
  exit 1
fi

BACKUP="../$(basename "$TARGET").backup.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
cp -a "$TARGET" "$BACKUP"

git filter-repo --path "$TARGET" --invert-paths --force

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$TARGET")"
cp -a "$BACKUP" "$TARGET"

# git-filter-repo removes origin as a safety measure. Re-add it manually.
git remote add origin https://github.com/MAZI2/PIFcamp26-Kaset-Net.git
git fetch origin

# Inspect before pushing.
git status
git log --oneline -- "$TARGET"

# Push only after you are sure.
git push --force-with-lease origin main
```


## History rewrite for every __pycache__ folder

```sh
git filter-repo \
  --path-glob '*/__pycache__/*' \
  --path-glob '__pycache__/*' \
  --invert-paths \
  --force

printf "\n__pycache__/\n*.pyc\n" >> .gitignore
git add .gitignore
git commit -m "ignore Python cache files"
```

Inspect before force pushing:

```sh
git status
git log --all -- '**/__pycache__/*'
```
